findings.text: Node layout holds a back pointer to the referencing slot, a small parent slot index, a fixed fan-out array of child slots, and a count of leaves under its branch.
Shortcut layout holds a back pointer, a parent slot, a target level to skip to, a next node pointer, and a flexible trailing index key sequence.

Edit transaction layout carries RCU linkage, array and operation pointers including ops for an excised subtree, leaf and dead leaf handles, small fixed arrays for new and excised metadata, a fan-out sized list of backpointer slots to rewrite plus their common target, a node and delta for count adjustment, two pointer assignments, one parent-slot assignment, and a segment cache one larger than fan-out.
Fan-out is 16 slots per node, with derived fan mask and level step values plus chunk mask and shift values derived from chunk size and word width.
Pointer tag uses bit 0 as leaf versus meta discriminator and bit 1 as node versus shortcut discriminator, with leaf zero and meta one, node zero and shortcut two.

Classification reports meta versus leaf and shortcut versus node by testing tag bits; conversions strip tag bits to recover an aligned object address or combine an address with tag bits to form a tagged pointer.
Bitmap sizing and initialization provide word-rounded size, zeroing, filling, copying, copying with tail clearing beyond the bit count, and copying with zero extension to a larger size.
Bitmap logic provides AND, OR, XOR, ANDNOT and complement, plus weighted OR and XOR that store the result and return its population count; AND and ANDNOT also report whether the result is non-empty.

Bitmap predicates provide equality, OR-equality against a third map, intersection, subset, emptiness, fullness, total weight, weight of conjunction, weight of difference, and weight over a start and end range.
Bitmap mutation provides setting and clearing a range, shifting right and left by a bit displacement, and selective replacement of old bits by new bits under a mask.

Scatter spreads successive source bits into destination positions named by a mask, while gather collects source bits at mask positions into successive destination bits; both start by clearing the destination.

Region handling releases, allocates, and searches power-of-two sized aligned regions; allocation fails when the range already holds bits and search scans successive regions until one allocates or reports exhaustion.
Narrow access reads or writes up to one machine word at an arbitrary bit offset, including a two-word spanning case, plus byte-wide and 32 and 64 bit array and 64-bit scalar transfer helpers.
Bit search provides first set bit, first clear bit, and next set bit from an offset, with an iterator macro that repeatedly advances to the next set position while inside the size.
Zero-area search with size, start, length and alignment mask forwards to an offset-capable variant using a zero base offset.
Fixed-width rotation is offered for 64, 32 and 16 bit words with shift masking to the width; population count dispatches on word size and bitmask order derives from find-last-set.

Single-bit operations dispatch through a helper that selects a constant-optimized form when number, address validity and pointee are all compile-time known; change, test-and-change, acquire-tested read, and conditional assign follow this pattern.
A compile-time check requires arch, generic, constant and internal spellings of a named bit operation to share one function type.
Bitmap word masks select bits from a start offset to the word end and the low valid bits of a partial final word; memory alignment and its mask gate bulk byte comparisons and fills.
Bit-count conversions round a bit count up to longs, 64-bit words, 32-bit words or bytes, and translate bytes to bits; a 64-bit value maps to one or two bitmap words depending on word width.

Many bitmap and find operations use a single-word inline path for small compile-time sizes and otherwise delegate to multi-word helpers; aligned constant ranges may use bulk memory operations instead.
Bits beyond the nominal count in the final word are not significant and must be masked on read-modify, comparison, weight and copy paths to avoid false differences or counts.
Narrow read and write treat an empty request or a width above one machine word as invalid, returning zero or doing nothing, and spanning accesses touch the following word so callers must provide it.
Ranged weight with start at or beyond end returns the end value rather than a weight, so callers must not interpret it as a population count.
